Half of the osmotic gradient across cells
tp: Excess dietary sodium appears to be a major factor in hypertension in some people. Excretion is mainly by the kidneys.

ww.Potassium: Potassium is the major intracellular cation and has little effect on osmotic pressure.
ww.Calcium: Calcium is mostly in bone and is not the main extracellular cation.

evidence: Sodium is the major cation of the extracellular fluid.

ans: Rising potassium, falling sodium or pressure
d: Falling potassium, rising sodium or pressure
tp: Aldosterone raises plasma water by reducing excretion of sodium and therefore water.

ww.Falling potassium, rising sodium or pres: These are the opposite conditions and would not call for aldosterone.
ww.High blood calcium: Calcium is regulated by PTH, calcitriol and calcitonin.

evidence: Aldosterone is released if blood levels of potassium increase, if blood levels of sodium severely decrease, or if blood pressure decreases.
